There are <=4*3^(n-1) such paths, giving (4/3)(6sqrt(p))^n. Summable bound plus countable Borel-Cantelli gives a uniform eventual cost lower bound from each root. Finite changes alter each simple path by at most their finite total magnitude; deletion only raises costs.

First S_n hits along its two arms enclose the only e traversal; any e-free inner competitor no dearer would replace it in the outer path and contradict strict preference, so s<H_n. Conditional on outside, ties t_e=H_n or H_infinity have probability zero by independence and nonatomicity. Intersecting {t_e<H_n} gives {t_e<H_infinity} off that null set, hence P(A_e|outside)=F(H_infinity).

The shell criterion H_n>=s+epsilon for every n follows by the same splice and diagonal arguments.
